title: Concurrency requires per-target single-flight for state-changing readiness
summary: Different targets may reconcile concurrently, but operations that can mutate the same target/generation/native repair state must be serialized or joined as one in-flight operation. The Audio fleet run exposed duplicate first-time Foreign Runtime rebuilds on the Oracle hosts when readiness was invoked twice.
invariants: Independent targets may deploy concurrently and retain distinct DeploymentResult objects.
Completion order across different targets must not alter desired state.
For the same target + generation + repair key, only one mutating readiness/rebuild operation should execute; concurrent callers should observe/join its state rather than spawn duplicate compilers.
Lock ownership and stale-lock recovery must be represented in deployment evidence.
BUILDING is not READY, and timeout/termination is not successful readiness.

provenance.claim: Permits independent-target concurrency with distinct results.
Operational run explicitly reports duplicate first-time native rebuilds caused by invoking readiness twice.
Shows two ensure_foreign_runtime/g++ trees on each Oracle host before redundant cleanup.
Shows A/B remained BUILDING after cleanup while other nodes had independent states.
